title: OxiGraphX predicted vacancy formation energies in high-entropy perovskites
summary: OxiGraphX, a graph neural network, predicted oxygen-vacancy formation energies for three high-entropy perovskite oxides that the authors synthesized. Experimental measurements reported 29% oxygen vacancies in BSL4B, 27% in SL4B and no detected vacancies in L4B, broadly tracking the predicted and DFT-calculated formation energies. The article contains inconsistent text assigning the relative oxygen-evolution overpotentials; this entry does not make that comparison.
ai_technology: OxiGraphX graph neural network for oxygen-vacancy formation-energy prediction
organization: University of North Carolina at Greensboro; University of North Georgia; Kennesaw State University; University of Texas at Austin; Brookhaven National Laboratory

source_review.scope: Primary publisher indexed full text, PMC full text and NCBI/PubMed metadata/affiliations. Disputed OER overpotential comparison omitted.

evidence.tested: Three high-entropy perovskite oxides were synthesized; oxygen-vacancy measurements reported 29% for BSL4B, 27% for SL4B and undetected for L4B. The article compares these measurements with OxiGraphX predictions and DFT calculations.
evidence.unknown: The source text conflicts on relative oxygen-evolution overpotentials, which are not included here. These tests do not establish device-level or industrial performance.
evidence.ai_role: OxiGraphX predicted oxygen-vacancy formation energies that informed selection of perovskite compositions for synthesis and comparison with measured vacancy content.
